epithet: of the Two Lands and the Jungle
ship: the Jade Canoe of the Itraa

morphology.compounding_rule: Egyptian construct-chains (Per-[god], Niut-[god], Ta-[land], Pa-[noun]) layered over Mayan [color|quality] + feature compounds (Chak-witz red-pyramid, softened to Chak-djew): the capital Ramaya (Ra-maya, the sun-jungle realm), Per-Tjuraa (temple of the sun) atop the Noh-Djewitz (the great temple-mountain).
morphology.patronymic_form: the Egyptian ruling house keeps the filiation 'sa' (son-of) and the theophoric construct; the Maya populace keep the ch'ib'al (lineage) and the aj-/ix- agentive on calendar-day names; the throne fuses both - a nesut who carries a Per- house-name and a ch'ib'al dynasty-count.

patterns.dungeons_ruins: buried solar-pyramids and vine-choked witz-cities: 'the Tomb of Per-aa [name]', 'the Sunken Per-netjer', 'the lost Djewitz of [ajaw]', 'the drowned Cenote of [name]'
patterns.military_units: the [god] Division and the Maya Holkan war-host: 'the Division of Rapetj', 'the Jaguar Holkan', 'the Feather-and-Sun Companies'
patterns.ships: solar-barques and jungle river-canoes: 'Barque of Tjuraa', 'the Jade Canoe of the Itraa', 'Beloved of the River'
patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]': 'The Jade Lotus', 'The Cacao and Crown', 'The Golden Quetzal'

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Egyptian reflexes PRIMARY (abydosian sample_deity_renames, the morphed-through-Egyptian-phonology set), Mayan morphs SECONDARY (family_mesoamerican.json theonym_sets.mayan), never real Egyptian/Maya gods (no Ra, Osiris, Isis; no Itzamna, Kukulkan, Chaac). Shared Agrippan pantheon, two registers. The solar god-king ideology and the funerary cult meet the Long-Count calendar and the witz-pyramid altar; the per-aa and the k'uhul ajaw both mediate the powers. Ramaya seeds/shifts Lawful, Neutral, or Chaotic (see worship_by_alignment).

clergy_ladder.9: Hem-netjer Aa (great prophet) / Ah-k'in Mai (high priest)

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as the kin of the great serpent Hefau (Egyptian) or the Maya demonized set, keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhu the City-Burner (Maya Marakab the War-Fire); Vacidus -> Wakedjet the Devouring Hefau (Maya Wakix the Devourer); Lusanto -> Lusandjaa the Hoard-Serpent (Maya Lusankaan).

holy_symbol_motifs.Djeroraa: the crook and flail crossed over a jade burial-mask
holy_symbol_motifs.Gaiandaa: the alluvial field beneath the stepped witz-pyramid
holy_symbol_motifs.Tjuraa: the sun-disc above the feather of right-order, set over the feathered-serpent glyph

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Per-netjer (god's-house/temple) of [power], often atop the witz (pyramid): 'the Per-netjer of Tjuraa', 'the K'uh-nah of Tulax atop the Djewitz'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified dead (the akhu and the Maya uchben) and the god-kings, venerated at tomb-pyramid and carved stela; 'the justified [name]' (maa-kheru) and the deified k'uhul ajaw ancestors.

sample_deity_renames.Delorum: Djeroraa (Maya Aj Delor) - lord of the peaceful dead
sample_deity_renames.Raptis: Rapetj (Maya Aj Raptaj) - the red hunter
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riaret (Maya Ix Rialtaj) - the mother, mercy
sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tjuraa (Maya Tulax) - the sun and right-order

religion.the_one: Atjernaa (Egyptian; Maya Aj Ternaj) - the hidden distant maker, honored not petitioned

worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Atjernaa - as the tyrant-gods to be defied; the bloodletting-rite feeds the devouring powers.
worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Atjernaa the One, Tjuraa the just sun, Gaiandaa the enduring, Numenaa the wise - and names the Chaotic powers the kin of the great serpent Hefau (and the Maya Lusankaan), warded; the solar law-of-maat and the Long-Count order bind alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the deified dead (the akhu and the Maya uchben), the god-kings and the day-lords; the great powers invoked at the per-netjer and atop the witz situationally, somewhat honored and somewhat feared

titles._tiers_note: Egyptian ladder, ascending, with the Maya substrate co-titles beneath. Hatia (mayor) barony; Wer-khaset (great-one of the frontier-land) march; Sepati/Sepat (nomarch/nome) county; Mer-mesha (army-overseer/general) duchy; Heqa-aa (great ruler) principality; Nesut (king) kingdom - shown as 'Pharaoh', the approved commonly-known foreign rank; Per-aa (lit. the Great House) empire over the Per-aat. The conquered witz-cities keep their Maya k'uhul ajaw (holy lord) and sajal (governor) and batab' (local chief) beneath the Egyptian crown. The hem-netjer priests and the ah-k'in day-keepers stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Egyptian and Maya registers (allowed).
titles.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.
titles.government: feudal (an Egyptian solar god-kingship over the Maya jungle pyramid-cities: the per-aa and his nesut-court at the crown, the heqa-aa princes and sepati nomarchs over the river-and-jungle provinces, the k'uhul-ajaw holy-lords and sajal governors of the witz-cities serving beneath; the hem-netjer temple-priesthood and the ah-k'in day-keepers order the calendar)
titles.heir: Sa-Nesut (king's son / crown prince); the baah-ch'ok (head-youth) of the Maya line

vassalage.fealty: Ankh (the living-oath) / Patan-t'an (Maya oath of service)
